messages:
Samira Patel: hey team, trying to finish onboarding. Okta enrollment keeps failing when I try to register my YubiKey. Browser shows 'No authenticator found'. I plugged it in, tapped it, nothing.
Elena (People Ops): welcome Samira! tagging @Mark from IT. Did you receive the Jamf enrollment and Google Workspace invites?
Samira Patel: yes i accepted Google invite earlier and set up 1Password. Jamf invite is showing 'pending' though.
okta-bot: Okta MFA enrollment could fail if device registration is blocked by device posture or MDM.
Mark (IT): @Samira can you confirm OS and browser? Also are you using a USB-A YubiKey with a USB-C adapter? Those adapters sometimes need a direct connection.
Samira Patel: macbook pro m1, macOS 13.4, Safari 16.3 and Chrome 117. I'm using a YubiKey 5 NFC with USB-C adapter. I tried both Safari and Chrome.
DevSec (Security): our baseline policy currently prefers WebAuthn via platform or external keys. If Jamf hasn't reported a managed device, the portal may try to register a passkey but block external keys until MDM. Mark, did we recently change enforcement for external tokens?
Mark (IT): checking. We tightened the new-hire flow to require platform authenticator (Touch ID) or company-managed FIDO keys. External personal keys are allowed only after MDM. That could explain the 'No authenticator' text if the browser negotiates a different set of allowed transports.
Samira Patel: oh — i used Touch ID to unlock my Mac but wasn't sure if that counts. How do I use Touch ID as the authenticator?
Mark (IT): In Safari there's an option to "Use Touch ID" when the OS prompts for a passkey. If Okta expects WebAuthn and the browser doesn't present a Touch ID option (or shows none), try System Preferences > Touch ID to ensure it's enabled for web authentication.
Samira Patel: Touch ID is enabled for unlocking; not sure about web auth. Also Jamf still shows pending.
Elena (People Ops): Jamf invite was sent an hour ago — maybe it got snoozed. Samira, do you want me to resend the Jamf invite and provision a temporary laptop if you prefer not to enroll your personal device?
Samira Patel: i'd like to avoid enrolling my personal laptop if possible. Could we use my phone as the authenticator?
DevSec (Security): platform authenticators on phones are acceptable as a temporary measure. If you have FaceID/TouchID on your phone and can use the Okta Verify app or platform passkeys, that should work. We can allow a 48-hour grace period to enroll a company device.
Mark (IT): I'll switch your Okta policy to allow mobile platform authenticators for 1 hour. Try re-enrolling and choose "Use a mobile device" or register via Okta Verify.
Samira Patel: ok trying now...
(3 minutes pass)
Samira Patel: success, registered via Okta Verify on my phone using FaceID. Enrollment completed and I can access console. Thanks!
1password-bot: Samira Patel has been added to the "redwood-engineering" vault. Follow the setup steps to import your secrets: https://1password.com/welcome
Elena (People Ops): great. Mark, please add Samira to #eng, #new-hires, and #oncall-readers. Also resend Jamf so she can enroll a company VM later.
Mark (IT): will do — Slack groups updated; Jamf invite resent. Samira you should get an email with a device enrollment link.
Samira Patel: got the Jamf link, i'll enroll the company VM later today. Thanks for the quick help everyone.
Raj (Manager): welcome Samira :tada: — ping me if you want a buddy pairing session this week for repo access and first tasks.
DevSec (Security): reminder: once you enroll the company VM, we'll revoke the temporary mobile auth allowance. You should be all set, but reach out if any ACLs are missing.
